issues.description: The problem materials are inconsistent about the collection type used for Farm.animals: the UML in the problem statement shows animals: List<Animal>, while the textual instructions explicitly require a Set implemented with HashSet. The provided solution implements animals as a List (ArrayList), and the template Farm.java does not define the field. This conflict will confuse students about whether to use a List or a Set and may cause mismatch with automated tests expecting one specific type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended collection type explicit and consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement UML to show animals: Set<Animal> (and keep the textual instruction), and update the solution and template to use private Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>(); adjust getter/setter signatures to use Set<Animal>; or (B) if a List is intended, change the textual instruction to require a List/ArrayList and remove the HashSet requirement. Ensure template Farm.java provides the correct field declaration and constructor initializing the chosen collection so students have a clear, consistent starting point.
